title: Recent progress on thermal transport in one-dimensional long-range interacting Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattice systems
authors: Daxing Xiong, Nianbei Li, Jie Chen
abstract: Long-range (LR) interactions are no longer just a theoretical idea: they can be engineered in several low-dimensional platforms and offer a new way to control heat transport. At the same time, they push beyond the standard picture developed mainly for short-range, momentum-conserving lattices. In this review, we consider one-dimensional Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT)-type lattices where LR effects enter mainly through a quartic anharmonic coupling that decays as a power law, characterized by an exponent σ. Our goal is to explain, in a unified way, how LR anharmonicity changes microscopic energy exchange, collective dynamics, and the macroscopic scaling laws of heat conduction-while also clarifying what is well established and what is still debated (For more details of the abstract, please see the main text and paper).
summary: This review analyzes heat transport in 1D lattices with long-range interactions, showing that the decay rate of these interactions ($\sigma$) dictates the transport regime. The findings reveal complex transitions between superdiffusion, normal diffusion, and subdiffusion, suggesting that LR coupling offers a tunable mechanism for controlling heat flow, potentially leading to thermal diodes.
main_problem: The paper investigates how long-range (LR) interactions fundamentally alter the mechanisms of heat transport in one-dimensional (1D) lattice systems, moving beyond established models for short-range interactions.
main_result: The transport regime is highly dependent on the LR decay exponent ($\sigma$): strong LR coupling leads to subdiffusion, while specific weak-LR regimes can approach normal diffusion or even ballistic transport.
method: The study employs theoretical analysis and numerical simulations using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics (NEMD) and the Green-Kubo formalism to calculate thermal conductivity and energy current correlations.
model_or_system: The model is a 1D Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT)-type lattice whose anharmonic coupling terms decay as a power law, $V(r) \propto 1/r^\sigma$. The focus is on the effects of this long-range, quartic anharmonicity.
key_observables: Thermal conductivity ($\kappa$), energy current autocorrelation function ($C_{JJ}(t)$), and spatiotemporal correlation functions of energy fluctuations ($ho_Q(m, t)$).
important_parameters: The LR decay exponent ($\sigma$), the system size ($N$), and the temperature/nonlinearity strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on comparing results from NEMD, Green-Kubo, and correlation function scaling, while acknowledging the challenge of ensemble inequivalence in LR systems.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature profile, the scaling of spatiotemporal correlations ($ho_Q(m, t)$) showing different growth rates (diffusive vs. ballistic), and the energy current autocorrelation function exhibiting negative correlations in certain regimes.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the theoretical framework, contrasting short-range vs. LR effects, systematically analyzes transport regimes based on $\sigma$ (e.g., $\sigma=2$, $1 < \sigma \le 3$, $0 \le \sigma \le 1$), and discusses the implications for thermal control.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it explores non-equilibrium dynamics and energy transport in complex many-body systems, touching upon concepts of non-integrability and anomalous diffusion that are central to modern condensed matter theory.
